instruments.name: data_loader_mnist
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether the MNIST dataset loaded by data.load_mnist matches the paper's own dataset (size, shape, label set, pixel range). A closed-book run that fell back to a synthetic corpus passed every gate and meant nothing; this fingerprint prevents that.
instruments.positive_test: data.load_mnist(0) returns x_train[50000,784] f32, y_train[50000] int64, x_val/x_test[10000,*], pixels in [0,1], labels exactly {0..9}, and the 3-vs-7 subset (load_mnist_3v7) contains only labels 3 and 7 mapped to y in {-1,+1} with +1==digit 3.
instruments.negative_test: A synthetic 65-vocabulary corpus or a wrong-shaped array (e.g. x_train[50000,784] of all-zeros, or labels missing class 8) would fail the shape/label-set/range assertions and be rejected.
instruments.requires_tools: network (MNIST IDX download from ossci-datasets S3 mirror)

instruments.name: data_loader_cifar10
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether CIFAR-10 loaded by data.load_cifar10 is the real dataset (50000+10000 images, 3072 dims after flatten, GCN-preprocessed to global std ~0.5).
instruments.positive_test: load_cifar10(0) returns x_train[45000,3072], x_val[5000,3072], x_test[10000,3072], labels {0..9}, and global std of x_train ~0.5 (within 0.04).
instruments.negative_test: A non-GCN-preprocessed array (global std ~ 1.0) or a wrong-dim array (e.g. 1024) fails the shape/std assertion.
instruments.status_note: In this run the CIFAR download stalled (cs.toronto.edu throttled the connection); the cifar_conv_maxout arm is marked BLOCKED rather than substituted with synthetic data.

instruments.name: numbers_gate
instruments.what_it_decides: For each claim in claims.json, whether the measured value (or sequence, for curve claims) satisfies the claim's assertion (value/ordering/existence/invariant/curve) at every seed. Renders pass/fail/blocked and writes claims_result.json with a produced_by stamp. A blocked HIGH claim makes the gate exit non-zero; a failed HIGH claim makes the gate exit non-zero; a grader that cannot run (malformed measured.json) raises a traceback rather than emitting a verdict.
instruments.positive_test: tests/test_numbers_gate.py::test_gate_positive_known_correct runs the gate (via sys.executable, in an isolated temp dir) on a measured.json where HIGH claim c03 holds and asserts c03 is verdicted pass and claims_result.json is stamped produced_by=numbers_gate.py.
instruments.negative_test: tests/test_numbers_gate.py::test_gate_negative_known_wrong runs the gate on a measured.json where c03 fails and asserts c03 is verdicted fail (not pass, not blocked); ::test_gate_blocked_metric_not_silent_pass asserts an absent arm yields verdict blocked, never a silent pass; ::test_gate_raises_on_unusable_input asserts a malformed measured.json crashes the gate with a traceback and non-zero exit and writes no claims_result.json (a grader that cannot run must raise, never return a negative verdict).
instruments.requires_tools: none (pure python; reads claims.json + measured.json). The gate runs in-process and is exercised through sys.executable (tests/test_numbers_gate.py), never by shelling out to bare `python` -- the 'python vs python3' mis-grading failure mode does not apply here.

instruments.name: logreg_analytic_equivalence
instruments.what_it_decides: c07: that FGSM is exact for logistic regression — the analytic closed form zeta(y*(eps*||w||_1 - w.x - b)) equals the actual adversarial loss under the paper's perturbation eta = -eps*sign(w) (tex:407-411).
instruments.positive_test: On a trained LogisticRegression3v7, |FGSM-form loss - analytic-form loss| < 1e-5 on a fixed batch (tests/test_invariants.py::test_logreg_fgsm_equals_analytic_form).
instruments.negative_test: If the analytic form used the wrong sign (e.g. +eps*||w||_1 instead of the paper's -sign(w) perturbation), the difference would be >> 1e-5 and the test/assertion fails.

instruments.name: fgsm_inf_norm
instruments.what_it_decides: That the FGSM perturbation satisfies ||eta||_inf == eps exactly (tex:309) with sign(0):=0 and no clipping (SPEC §4.9).
instruments.positive_test: attack.fgsm produces x_adv with max|eta| == eps and every perturbed pixel exactly eps (tests/test_invariants.py::test_fgsm_inf_norm_equals_eps, test_fgsm_no_clipping).
instruments.negative_test: A clipping implementation that clamps x_adv to [0,1] would fail test_fgsm_no_clipping; a scaled (non-sign) perturbation would fail the exact-eps assertion.

instruments.name: degeneracy_check
instruments.what_it_decides: That the method at its no-op setting (adversarial eps=0, noise eps=0, L1 coef=0) reproduces the baseline training EXACTLY (bit-identical weights). The cheapest real correctness evidence: catches a mis-wired adversarial/noise loop in seconds.
instruments.positive_test: tests/test_degeneracy.py: a model trained with adversarial eps=0 has weights bit-identical to the baseline (torch.equal), and identical val_err curves.
instruments.negative_test: An adversarial-training loop that leaks gradients through sign, or consumes RNG even at eps=0, produces different weights and the degeneracy assertion fails.

instruments.name: rubbish_any_prob_threshold
instruments.what_it_decides: Whether a model assigns any class probability > 0.5 to Gaussian rubbish inputs (tex:905-911). For softmax-top: max_k p_k > 0.5; for sigmoid-top / RBF (rows need not sum to 1): any p_k > 0.5.
instruments.positive_test: eval.rubbish_eval on a softmax model: rubbish_err in [0,100]; class_shares keys '0'..'9' sum to 100 (when mistakes exist). On an RBF net far from data, rubbish_err ~ 0.
instruments.negative_test: A bug that used argmax-confidence > 0.5 on a softmax (always true, since max prob >= 0.1) would report ~100% rubbish_err for a well-trained model that is actually robust — caught by the RBF-zero assertion.
